title: Compile-Time Constants as Configuration
pattern: Hardcoding tuning parameters (e.g., pool sizes, timeout limits, or IP addresses) as compile-time constants instead of reading them dynamically from external sources.
why_bad: Under stress (e.g., an outage requiring immediate adjustment of a connection pool size to zero or one to stop overloading a database), operations must wait for a full build, compile, and rolling deploy cycle, turning a 5-minute fix into a multi-hour outage.
detection: Compile-time constants used to set connection pool sizing, socket timeouts, or server endpoint URLs.
counterexample: True logical constants like math limits or default internal buffer capacities.
fix: Load operational configurations from external environment variables, files, or dynamic services.
